free_tier.stated: unlimited tunnels and unmetered transit; 1,000 tunnels per account

per_object_cap.stated: 100 MB proxied request body on Free and Pro (413), 200 MB Business

retention.stated: not applicable: the tunnel and its hostname persist

egress.terms: unmetered; no bandwidth figure appears among the account limits

chaining: the serving chain for a real hostname: a domain on Cloudflare nameservers -> a named tunnel -> an origin that cannot open a port. Composes with Oracle Always Free as the origin and with R2 behind it, and the scarce link is the domain.

limits.value: the hostname must be a zone on Cloudflare nameservers
100 MB proxied request body on Free and Pro
125 s proxy read timeout and 30 s proxy write timeout, both 524

identity_cost.detail: a Cloudflare account plus a domain delegated to Cloudflare nameservers

reliability_note: community reports describe about 20 Mbit/s on tunnel transfers; not reproduced here

evidence.proved: 1,000 tunnels per account, 25 replicas per tunnel, 50,000 routes, and no bandwidth figure anywhere on the page
Proxy Read Timeout 125 s and Proxy Write Timeout 30 s, both returning 524
Cloudflare staff, 2022-06-21: 'There are no bandwidth limits'

notes: 'Unmetered' is a documented absence rather than a quota, so it is not multiplied here. The census cited the account-limits page for the 100 MB figure; that page does not contain it.

extras.transit_note: cloudflared dials out and Cloudflare relays the request and response bytes

binding_note: the domain is the only paid element and the gate; the 100 MB body cap binds writes, not reads.
interface_detail: cloudflared tunnel run; the hostname is a record on a zone the client owns
limits_note: counts of things, not rates, so no vocabulary kind names them: 1,000 cloudflared tunnels per account and 25 active replicas per tunnel; 50,000 routes per account, shared with Cloudflare Mesh
